name: Shopify
description: Shopify is an all-in-one commerce platform that lets businesses build an online store, process payments, and sell across web, mobile, social, and in-person channels.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.notes: $29/month equivalent when billed yearly; $39 month-to-month. Shopify lists a 2% third-party payment-provider fee when not using Shopify Payments.

tiers.name: Grow
tiers.notes: $79/month equivalent when billed yearly; $105 month-to-month. Up to 5 staff accounts; 1% third-party payment-provider fee.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.notes: $299/month equivalent when billed yearly; $399 month-to-month. Up to 15 staff accounts; 0.6% third-party payment-provider fee.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.notes: Starts at $2,300/month on a 3-year term; more complex business structures can use a variable platform fee.

best_for: Positioned for businesses of all sizes — from solo entrepreneurs launching their first store to large enterprises.
features: Website builder with themes and AI-assisted design

alternatives.name: BigCommerce
alternatives.description: An ecommerce platform supporting both B2C and B2B storefronts, marketplaces, and social commerce channels.
alternatives.best_for: Businesses needing B2B account/pricing workflows alongside a standard storefront.

alternatives.name: WooCommerce
alternatives.description: An open-source ecommerce platform built as a WordPress plugin, giving merchants full control over their store.
alternatives.best_for: WordPress users/developers wanting full customization ownership.

cons: Shopify's lowest displayed Basic price requires annual billing; month-to-month Basic is $39 instead of the $29 annual-billing equivalent.
If a merchant uses a third-party payment provider instead of Shopify Payments, Shopify lists additional transaction fees of 2% on Basic, 1% on Grow, and 0.6% on Advanced.
Shopify Plus starts at $2,300/month on a 3-year term, so the enterprise tier has a much larger minimum commitment than the self-serve plans.
